claims.text: The initial Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is an as-solidified, single-phase solid solution.
FeNiCrMn is a Co-free derivative of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Dynamic loading induces transient local short-range ordering in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The stress-induced local ordering produces measurable lattice distortions.
High strain rates and/or low temperatures promote a reversible transition toward a short-range-ordered state.
Short-range ordering alters the atomic energy landscape and impedes dislocation motion in a pinning-like fashion.
Ordering-mediated impediment of dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Ordering-mediated changes in dislocation mobility enhance or modulate strain hardening.
At slower strain rates and higher temperatures, thermal agitation prevents or reverses the proposed ordering.
When ordering is absent or reversed, the alloy returns toward conventional solid-solution deformation behavior.
Stress-induced ordering will generate reversible diffraction peak broadening or splitting and TEM-visible local ordering.
At high strain rates and low temperatures, the Co-free alloy will have greater yield strength and strain hardening than the stated baseline.
The structural and mechanical signatures of ordering will diminish as strain rate decreases or temperature increases.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can serve as a baseline exhibiting minimal or no stress-induced ordering.
Slow-deformation and high-temperature testing of Co-free FeNiCrMn can serve as a no-ordering baseline.
The proposed mechanism is active over strain rates of 10^-4 to 10^-1 s^-1 and temperatures from cryogenic levels to approximately 500 K.
Outside the stated strain-rate and temperature range, conventional deformation mechanisms operate without transient local ordering.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the mechanism is active throughout 10^-4–10^-1 s^-1 and from cryogenic temperature to about 500 K, while the mechanism and baseline state that slow-rate and high-temperature portions of that same range prevent or reverse ordering and represent a no-ordering baseline.

The comparison baseline is not singular: it alternates between a compositionally different equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy and the same Co-free alloy tested under slow/high-temperature conditions. Consequently, the claimed effect cannot be attributed uniquely to Co removal or to loading conditions.
